abberufen.why: Bare 'withdraw' is the vaguest reading of candidate 0 and points at withdrawing money/troops/statements, none of which abberufen covers; the verb is recalling a person from an office or post (candidate 1, einen Botschafter abberufen).

abblasen.why: The dominant modern sense is calling off an event or plan (candidate 2, das Spiel/den Streik abblasen); the shipped literal 'blow off/blow clear' (candidate 0) is a technical blowing sense the learner will rarely meet.

abdrehen.why: 'veer' (candidate 0) is a narrow nautical/aviation sense; the everyday meaning is shutting off a supply at a valve or switch (candidate 4, das Wasser/Gas abdrehen). Both proposed words are true synonyms.

abfeiern.why: My independent gloss reached the standard workplace sense (candidate 2, Überstunden abfeiern), which dictionaries list first; the shipped 'celebrate, praise, love' is the newer colloquial-slang sense (candidate 0) whose lead word 'celebrate' reads as plain feiern. Both are sourced, so no unsourced-wording penalty applies.

abführen.why: 'take away' is a truncation of candidate 0 that dropped the '(someone in police custody)' parenthetical, leaving a gloss that reads as wegnehmen; abführen is leading a person away under escort (candidate 0).

abgleichen.why: The shipped 'verify congruence' is lifted from a garbled kaikki entry (candidate 0, 'to but check or collate') and is not English anyone uses; abgleichen is comparing data or accounts to bring them into agreement (Daten/Kontostände abgleichen).

abhauen.why: The live everyday meaning is to clear off or run away (candidate 1, Hau ab!, er ist abgehauen); the shipped 'cut off' is the older literal hewing sense (candidate 0) surviving mainly in fixed phrases.

ablenken.why: The core sense is distracting someone or their attention (candidate 1, jemanden ablenken); bare 'divert' (candidate 0) reads as redirecting traffic or a river, which is umleiten, inviting the wrong use. The proposal keeps 'divert' and adds the primary sense.

ablesen.why: The shortening cut '(take a reading)' from candidate 0, collapsing the gloss into the base verb lesen; ablesen never means reading a book, it is taking a reading off a gauge (den Zaehlerstand ablesen).

abrichten.why: The everyday meaning is training an animal (candidate 1, einen Hund abrichten); bare 'drill' (candidate 0) reads first as boring a hole, which is bohren, and would teach the wrong verb.

abstechen.old: cut off, cut out, carve out
abstechen.why: The shipped 'cut off, cut out, carve out' renders the specialized spade sense (candidate 0, Torf abstechen) and reads as a synonym of abschneiden, which it is not; the ordinary sense is to stab, especially to death (candidate 1, ein Schwein abstechen).

absterben.why: absterben is the ordinary verb for tissue, plants, or limbs dying off (candidate 2, abgestorbene Aeste; mir ist der Fuss abgestorben); 'atrophy' is both more technical and semantically off, since atrophy is wasting from disuse (verkuemmern).

abtreiben.why: In essentially all contemporary non-nautical use abtreiben means the abortion sense (candidates 1 and 2); the shipped 'go/be sent off course' (candidate 0) is the drift sense restricted to boats and swimmers, the wrong sense to have chosen.

abtreten.why: 'kick away' (candidate 0) is a marginal reading; the senses a learner meets are stepping down from office (candidate 4, von einem Amt abtreten) and ceding rights or territory (Rechte/Gebiete abtreten), which are related relinquish senses rather than opposed ones.

abwägen.why: abwägen is figurative only, weighing options against one another (Vor- und Nachteile abwägen); bare 'weigh' (candidate 0, once disambiguated by the dropped '(to determine the intrinsic value or merit)') collides directly with abwiegen, which this corpus glosses 'weigh, weigh out'.

abwählen.why: Shipped 'deselect' (candidate 0) is the narrow computing/checkbox reading; in ordinary German abwählen means voting an officeholder out (candidate 1, eine Regierung abwählen) or dropping a school subject, which a learner given only 'deselect' would miss. The proposal keeps 'deselect' and adds the political sense.

anfallen.why: The reading a learner meets is the impersonal one (candidate 3, anfallende Kosten/Arbeit/Daten), i.e. costs or work that arise or accrue; the shipped 'set upon, attack suddenly' (candidate 0) is a literary and largely dated sense.

angeloben.why: angeloben is chiefly Austrian and its ordinary use is the swearing-in of soldiers and officeholders (candidate 2, Angelobung); the shipped 'vow' is the base-verb sense of geloben, not what a learner meets angeloben in.

anhaben.old: wear, have on see usage notes
anhaben.why: The trailing 'see usage notes' is Wiktionary editorial scaffolding that survived the shortening of candidate 0; it is not part of the meaning and reads as broken English. The remaining 'wear, have on' is correct.

anhalten.why: 'stop, continue' joins two opposite actions under the house style's synonym comma, asserting something false; the sense a learner meets is 'stop' (candidate 0, er hielt das Auto an), and 'halt' is a true synonym.

anhängen.why: The everyday sense is physical or digital attachment (eine Datei anhängen, einen Anhänger anhängen), entirely absent from kaikki's entry here; the shipped 'weigh on, burden' renders only the far rarer figurative dative reading (candidate 0). Attach is the common sense the shipped gloss omits, so the fix is a rewrite.

anklagen.old: indict by the findings of a jury)
anklagen.why: The shipped 'indict by the findings of a jury)' is a mangled shortening of candidate 0, cutting the middle of the parenthetical and leaving a dangling clause with an unbalanced closing paren; anklagen means to accuse or, in legal register, to charge or indict.

anleiten.why: 'guide or to train' is candidate 0 pasted with only the first 'to' stripped, leaving a dangling infinitive marker ungrammatical in the bare-verb-phrase style; anleiten is to instruct or give guidance to someone (Anleitung).

anvertrauen.why: The shipped 'entrust in various ways' is kaikki's sense-group umbrella, not a definition: candidate 0 ends in a colon and the sub-senses follow. The plain meaning is entrust (candidate 1).

aufatmen.why: aufatmen (erleichtert aufatmen) denotes breathing out in relief; the relief is the meaning, not an overtone. The sole candidate 'breathe again' is a literal auf+atmen calque that reads as resuming breathing (wieder atmen). My independent gloss matches the proposal.

aufbleiben.why: The leading 'wake' in candidate index 0 is the archaic vigil sense; in first position a comma-joined 'wake' maps aufbleiben onto aufwachen/aufwecken, which it never means. Dropping it leaves the two genuine synonyms.

auferwecken.why: auferwecken is the elevated causative of auferstehen (Lazarus auferwecken); the sole candidate 'raise up, awaken' is vague and 'awaken' collides with aufwecken. My independent gloss matches, and it mirrors the app's existing auferstehen gloss.

auflehnen.why: sich auflehnen is essentially always reflexive and means to rebel (candidate index 1). The shipped 'lean on' is the marginal physical reading and collides with anlehnen; it is genuinely the wrong sense to have chosen. My independent gloss matches.

aufschieben.why: The overwhelmingly dominant everyday sense is temporal (die Entscheidung aufschieben; Aufschieberitis), candidate index 1. The shipped 'push open' is a narrow literal reading restricted to sliding objects; it leaves the learner unable to read the ordinary use.

aufschlagen.why: The reviewer is right that 'pitch, serve' is a poor choice: 'pitch' reads as baseball or pitching a tent, and the tennis-serve sense is narrow. But the proposal 'open (a book), serve' joins two distinct senses with a comma, so I ship the single clean everyday sense (candidate index 3).

aufsetzen.why: The shortening dropped the qualifier that carried the meaning (candidate index 0, 'put on something worn on the head'). Bare 'put on' invites use for clothing generally, which takes anziehen; one setzt a Hut or Brille auf, not Schuhe. My independent gloss matches.

aufsteigen.why: The core sense is upward motion (Rauch/Ballon steigt auf), from which the very common promotion sense (beruflich, in die Bundesliga aufsteigen) follows; that is candidate index 2. Shipped 'get on, mount' is a narrow application that gives the learner no access to either. My independent gloss matches.

aufstören.why: 'Pattern up' is not English and names no action; it is a corrupt Wiktionary entry taken verbatim as the sole candidate. aufstören means to rouse/startle out of rest (aufscheuchen, Wild aufstören), figuratively to stir up. A learner can recover nothing from the shipped gloss.

auftreiben.why: The dominant modern use is procuring something with difficulty (Wo soll ich Geld auftreiben?), candidate index 3. The shipped 'bloat' (index 0) is a marginal sense; as a bare gloss a learner would use auftreiben for distending a belly, not finding something. My independent gloss matches.

aufwarten.why: The shipped 'serve, wait' is the dated servant sense, and bare 'wait' reads as warten (wait for), the wrong verb entirely. The living construction mit etwas aufwarten means to offer/present (candidate index 2), which the proposal captures.

aufzeichnen.why: The reviewer is right that 'plot, chart' (index 0) is a narrow graph-paper sense and the everyday meaning is recording (eine Sendung aufzeichnen, index 2). But the proposal 'record, draw' joins two distinct senses with a comma, so I ship the single dominant sense.

ausbringen.why: The shortening cut the qualifier from candidate index 0 ('utter something others echo') — the toast sense, einen Trinkspruch ausbringen. Bare 'raise' reads as heben or erhöhen, which ausbringen does not mean. My independent gloss matches.

ausholen.why: The kaikki parenthetical that carried the meaning ('draw back the arm to punch', candidate index 0) was dropped; bare 'haul off' reads in English as carrying something away. German ausholen is winding the arm back before a blow. My independent gloss matches.

auslernen.why: auslernen specifically means completing a vocational apprenticeship (sie hat ausgelernt = she is now fully trained). The sole candidate 'finish learning' is a literal calque that fits only 'man lernt nie aus' and would generate ungrammatical uses like 'ich habe das Buch ausgelernt'. My independent gloss matches.

auslesen.why: In modern English 'cull' (index 0) is dominated by the selective-slaughter sense, which auslesen never carries. The reading a learner meets is 'select, pick out' (index 2, cf. Auslese). The one-word shipped gloss teaches the wrong action; my independent gloss matches.

ausscheiden.why: The shipped 'secrete' (index 0) is technical and imprecise — ausscheiden is excretion, not secretion (that is absondern). The sense a learner meets is dropping out of a competition or leaving a post (index 2). My independent gloss matches.

ausscheren.why: 'Sheer, sheer out' (index 0) is nautical jargon opaque to a learner, and 'sheer' collides with the far more familiar adjective. The everyday sense is a vehicle pulling out of line / changing lanes, figuratively breaking ranks (index 1). My independent gloss matches.

ausschreiben.why: Bare 'advertise' defaults in English to promoting a product, which ausschreiben never means (that is werben für). The verb puts a position or contract out for open application (eine Stelle ausschreiben, indices 1/3/5). The restored qualifier fixes a shortening defect; my independent gloss matches.

austrinken.why: The shipped 'empty' (index 0) strips the drinking component that distinguishes austrinken from leeren; a learner would use it for emptying a box. The verb means to finish one's drink to the last drop (index 2). My independent gloss matches.

bedingen.old: have agreed upon as a contractual term
bedingen.why: The shipped phrase is the archaic legal/contractual sense (index 0), surviving today mainly in sich ausbedingen and the obsolete strong forms bedang/bedungen; living bedingen is causal (das bedingt hohe Kosten; bedingt durch), candidate indices 1 and 2. It is also unusable as a short gloss. My independent gloss matches.

befallen.why: 'affect' is neutral-causation and collides with beeinflussen/beeinträchtigen; befallen is the verb of disease, pests, and sudden emotion seizing a subject. The proposed 'afflict, infest' draws on candidate 1 ('to seize') and candidate 2 ('to infest').

befühlen.why: 'palpate' (the sole candidate) is opaque medical jargon and is really the gloss for abtasten/palpieren; befühlen is everyday German for running one's hands over something, so the register mismatch misrepresents an ordinary verb. 'feel, touch' is the plain sense in house style.

beikommen.why: Shipped 'come here' is kaikki's regional (landschaftlich) reading; standard beikommen takes the dative and means to get at or cope with something (dem Problem beizukommen), which is candidate 1 ('to deal with'). This is a regional sense chosen where the common one was available.

beklagen.why: Leading with 'pity' points at bemitleiden, and the comma in 'pity, lament' asserts a false synonymy between non-synonyms; beklagen is to lament, bemoan, or deplore (Opfer beklagen). The proposed 'lament, deplore' are true synonyms and match the 'lament' half of candidate 0.

belachen.why: 'belaugh' is an unusable Wiktionary calque of the German prefix imported verbatim from candidate 0, not English a learner will ever meet. 'laugh at' names the sense completely.

bemeistern.why: bemeistern means to get a difficulty under control (seine Angst bemeistern); 'dominate' names holding power over people, the action of beherrschen/dominieren, which the verb does not denote. kaikki's sole candidate 'to dominate' is itself the weak rendering, but I independently know the master/overcome sense.

bepflanzen.why: The be- prefix makes the ground the object (ein Beet bepflanzen); bare 'plant' collapses the verb into base pflanzen and invites the error einen Baum bepflanzen. candidate 0's '(supply with plants)' rider preserves exactly the distinction the shortening dropped.

berücken.why: 'ensnare' is the obsolete hunting sense (catching game in a Rücke); in all living use berücken means to enchant or charm (berückend schön), which is candidate 1 ('to captivate'). This is an archaic sense shipped where the current one was available.

bescheiden.old: confer the decision or fate formally
bescheiden.why: 'Confer the decision or fate formally' is a truncation of candidate 0 that is not usable English — you do not confer a decision on someone. The transitive Amtsdeutsch verb (jemanden abschlägig bescheiden) means to notify someone of an official ruling, which the proposed gloss states cleanly.

beschenken.why: 'endow' in English means to fund an institution or be furnished with a quality — neither is what beschenken does. jemanden beschenken is the everyday word for giving somebody presents, matching candidate 1 ('to present, to gift').

beschicken.why: 'commit' is not usable English for this verb (it pulls toward committing a crime/resources), and the shipped gloss omits the frequent technical sense of charging a furnace or machine. candidate 1 ('to procure, to supply, to load, to furnish') groups sending and loading under one provisioning sense, so the proposed 'send to, load' is a coherent facet-pair, not false synonymy.

beschneiden.why: Circumcision is a real but specialized application; the everyday senses are horticultural (Hecken beschneiden) and figurative (Rechte/Freiheiten beschneiden), the latter among the verb's most frequent collocations, and Duden lists trimming first. candidate 1 ('to trim; to prune') plus the well-attested curtail reading is the sense a learner meets.

bespringen.why: 'synonym of begatten' is a Wiktionary cross-reference, not a meaning, and it points at an untranslated target — leaked dictionary apparatus. bespringen is the animal-husbandry term for a male mounting a female to breed; 'mount (of animals)' is English about the verb.

bestecken.why: 'get stuck' is the rare intransitive reading with the opposite valency (a plough that comes to a standstill); the living verb is transitive — einen Kranz mit Blumen bestecken — which is candidate 1. As shipped, the gloss names an action the verb does not perform.

bestärken.why: bestärken takes a person and reinforces them in a belief or resolve (jemanden in seiner Meinung bestärken); bare 'strengthen'/'fortify' name physical strengthening (stärken/verstärken) and invite die Mauer bestärken. The proposed gloss is assembled from attested senses — 'reinforce' from candidate 1 and 'encourage' from candidate 0.

beweinen.why: The sense is right but this is kaikki's unfiltered four-synonym list (candidate 0), and 'beweep' is Shakespearean, not modern English. 'mourn, cry over' names the meaning within house-style length.

dahinsterben.why: 'die' is the gloss for plain sterben and drops the dahin- prefix's contribution; like dahinsiechen and dahinvegetieren, this verb names a gradual dying — wasting away or a population dying off over time — not the event of death. The prefix sense is not in kaikki's lone candidate but is a real, systematic feature of dahin- verbs.

daransetzen.why: Shortening stripped candidate 0's parentheticals, leaving 'risk, not spare, make, use' — four disjoint bare verbs and a fragment that name no action. The verb lives in alles daransetzen / seine ganze Kraft daransetzen: to stake something on an aim, to devote all effort to it.

darniederliegen.why: 'be sick' (candidate 0) misleads twice: in British English it reads as 'vomit', and the elevated verb applies well beyond illness (die Wirtschaft liegt darnieder). The sense is lying prostrate, laid low, in a slump, closer to candidate 1 ('to languish').

dazukommen.why: 'arrive' collides with ankommen and misses the core additive meaning: to join something in progress or, very commonly, to be added on top (dazu kommt, dass …), which is candidate 1 ('to be added'). 'join, be added' are two facets of the one accession sense.

draufgeben.why: 'add of something' is ungrammatical English produced by deleting the '(on top)' parenthetical from candidate 0. 'add on top' restores the meaning (etwas draufgeben).

durchbringen.why: Shipped 'be able to bring through' keeps candidate 0's modal scaffolding ('be able to'), which is dictionary framing, not part of the verb, so it names no action a learner can attach. The senses actually met — getting someone through an illness/exam/bill, and supporting or keeping fed — cluster in candidates 2–5, and 'get through, pull through' captures them.

durchfallen.why: The importer took the compositional literal sense, but in use durchfallen almost always means to fail an exam or audition (durch die Prüfung fallen), candidate 1 ('to fail, to not pass'). English 'fall through' additionally reads idiomatically as a plan collapsing (scheitern), which the verb does not mean.

durchschauen.why: candidate 0 is 'to see through (e.g. a window, telescope)'; the dropped parenthetical was doing the disambiguating work. Bare 'see through' idiomatically means detecting a deception — the stress-shifted inseparable durchscháuen (jemanden durchschauen), not this literal separable verb — so 'look through' names the intended sense unambiguously, as durchblicken is glossed elsewhere in the corpus.

einbilden.why: Candidate 0 is literally 'to imagine (falsely)' and the shortening dropped the parenthetical that carries the entire distinction from neutral sich vorstellen; restoring it is a correction, not an invention.

einkehren.why: 'sojourn' (candidate 0) is archaic and reads as a general extended stay; the living sense is stopping off at an inn during a journey (im Gasthaus einkehren), a strong-grounds archaic-lead case even though the correct sense is absent from the candidate list.

einkommen.why: 'earn' (candidate 0) names verdienen's transitive action and licenses the ungrammatical *ich komme Euro ein; einkommen is intransitive and formal (eingekommene Gelder), so the shipped gloss names an action the verb does not denote.

einreisen.why: 'travel' belongs to reisen, and the shipped comma presents it as synonymous with bare 'enter' (which is betreten/eintreten); einreisen specifically means crossing a border into a country — the ein- is the whole content.

einschreiben.why: The literal inscribe sense (candidate 0) is the rarest of the three; the everyday verbal use is reflexive sich einschreiben = enroll/register at a university (candidate 2), so shipping the rare sense where a common one was available warrants the swap.

einschulen.old: instruct for a specific position, task
einschulen.why: The shipped gloss is the chiefly Austrian workplace sense (train someone for a job) written as a dictionary paraphrase; standard German einschulen means enrolling a child in school (candidate 1, cf. Einschulung), the dominant everyday meaning.

einstellen.why: 'set, hire' joins two unrelated senses across a comma that house style reads as synonymy; the proposal commits to one coherent sense, adjust/set (candidate 1), whose parts are true synonyms.

einwenden.why: 'raise, make' are the bare verbs of candidate 0 with their objects ('an objection to', 'an argument against') stripped, so they name no action a learner can attach; einwenden means to object (dagegen ist nichts einzuwenden).

einüben.why: Leaked apparatus: the shipped gloss carries a stray '#' sense-separator and the unstripped infinitival 'to practice / practise' from candidate 0; 'practice, rehearse' is clean English about the verb.

entbinden.old: see a woman through childbirth, deliver
entbinden.why: The shipped attendant-perspective paraphrase ('see a woman through childbirth') is a dictionary sense-description rather than a gloss; the everyday learner-met use takes the mother as subject = give birth (candidates 1 and 2, 'Wann entbindest du?').

entfahren.why: Bare 'escape' (candidate 0) points at entfliehen/entkommen, which entfahren does not mean; its living sense is the involuntary utterance (ein Fluch entfuhr ihm), candidate 1 'to slip out (someone's) mouth'.

entrücken.why: 'translate' (candidate 0) is the archaic theological sense and the single worst false friend in a German app — a learner reads übersetzen; the living sense is carrying someone away or enrapturing mentally/spiritually (candidates 1 and 2).

entschlafen.why: Leading with 'fall asleep' (candidate 0) invites confusion with einschlafen; modern entschlafen is only the euphemism for dying (sanft entschlafen), so 'pass away' names the sole living sense and drops the archaic literal one.

ergehen.why: 'forms the perfect with sein' (candidate 0) is leaked Wiktionary auxiliary-selection apparatus, not a meaning; ergehen's living impersonal use is 'fare' (Wie ist es dir ergangen?), candidate 2.

erhoffen.why: kaikki's semicolon-separated 'hope (for); desire; want' (candidate 0) flattened to commas presents 'desire, want' as synonyms of the verb; erhoffen means specifically to hope for, and 'want' wrongly invites substitution for wollen.

erlöschen.why: The candidate list holds only the transitive extinguish sense, but strong erlöschen (erlosch, ist erloschen) is intransitive — a flame goes out, a right or contract lapses; 'extinguish' licenses the ungrammatical *ich erlösche das Feuer, so this corrects a wrong-transitivity import.

erraten.why: 'determine through advice or empathy' (candidate 0) is an archaic sense preserved from raten (advise) that barely reads as an English verb meaning; the only living sense is 'guess correctly' (candidate 1, Du hast es erraten).

erstatten.why: 'file' is a stranded fragment of the collocations Anzeige/Bericht erstatten, uninterpretable on its own and comma-joined to the unrelated 'reimburse'; candidate 0 explicitly gives reimburse/refund as the free-object sense.

ersterben.why: Bare 'die' duplicates sterben and points at the wrong register; modern ersterben is the figurative fade-out (der Lärm erstarb, das Lächeln erstarb), candidate 1 'to die away, to gradually stop'.

erwachsen.why: 'grow up' is aufwachsen (first in kaikki because the participle became the adjective 'adult'); the finite verb erwachsen means to arise or spring from (daraus erwuchsen Probleme), candidates 1 and 4, so 'grow up' sends the learner to the wrong verb.

erziehen.why: kaikki's 'to nurture' (index 0, taken verbatim) is the fostering/caring sense of pflegen or hegen, not the formative raising erziehen denotes (Kinder erziehen, Erziehung). 'raise, bring up' is the ordinary meaning even though kaikki lists only nurture/educate.

festfrieren.why: fest- is the whole content: to freeze fast to something (das Boot ist am Ufer festgefroren), not surface-icing, which is zufrieren or vereisen. Shipped 'ice over, freeze' names an action the verb does not denote despite kaikki's index 0.

festhalten.why: The comma makes 'hold on' and 'record' read as synonyms, but they are candidate senses 0/1 (grip) versus 5 (document); commit to the physical grip sense a learner meets first and most often.

feststehen.why: kaikki lists only the literal fest+stehen 'stand firm', which is standhalten/festbleiben; feststehen is predicated of facts and arrangements (Der Termin steht fest) = be settled, established. Shipped teaches the wrong verb for acts of resolve.

fortfahren.why: 'continue' is candidate index 2/3 and the dominant modern sense (mit der Arbeit fortfahren, Fahren Sie fort); the vehicular departure sense the shipped gloss features is dated, displaced in modern usage by wegfahren/losfahren.

fortgehen.old: continue, go on, keep on, carry on
fortgehen.why: The primary sense is departure, a straight synonym of weggehen (candidate index 1); shipped features the rarer impersonal 'continue' (die Arbeit geht fort) and its four crowded synonyms edge out the sense a learner needs.

fortschleifen.old: synonym of wegschleifen: to drag away
fortschleifen.why: Leaked dictionary apparatus: 'synonym of wegschleifen:' is a cross-reference to another German verb, not English about this one, and it fronts a word the learner has no reason to know. Only the tail 'drag away' (candidate index 0) is a gloss.

freimachen.why: 'put a stamp on' is the technical postal frankieren sense a learner will essentially never meet; the live senses are clearing or freeing something up (candidate index 1, die Straße freimachen).

freuen.why: The comma pairs converse valencies — reflexive 'be happy' (candidate index 1) with transitive 'please' (candidate index 0) — and 'be happy, please' misreads as an imperative with a politeness word; commit to the reflexive sich freuen sense a learner meets first.

fällen.why: Bare 'pass' is intelligible only if one already knows ein Urteil fällen and reads as a false second synonym of 'fell'; the core sense is felling a tree (candidate index 0).

geraten.why: The comma joins 'get into' (candidate index 3, in Panik/Schwierigkeiten geraten) with 'turn out' (candidate index 0, der Kuchen ist gut geraten), two different senses; commit to the dominant unintentional-arrival sense with true synonyms.

gewarten.why: 'await or wait for' is lifted kaikki alternation phrasing, a dictionary 'or' no other gloss in the corpus uses; the sense is right, and house style lists the synonyms with commas (candidate index 0).

haushalten.why: Shipped 'run a household' is the dated standalone reading; modern usage is overwhelmingly mit etwas haushalten = use a resource sparingly (mit den Kräften/dem Geld haushalten), which is candidate index 1 and attested, not invented.

herausbrechen.why: Shipped 'burst out' is the narrow figurative frame es brach aus ihm heraus (candidate index 0) and standing alone misreads as burst out laughing; the literal sense a learner meets — forcibly breaking a piece out, or a piece breaking off — is candidate index 1.

herausgeben.why: 'hand out' names verteilen/austeilen, not herausgeben (surrender or give back, e.g. Geld herausgeben — candidate index 1); the safe fix keeps the correct 'publish' and replaces the misleading term with its synonym 'issue' (candidate index 2).

heraushalten.new: keep out of, stay out of
heraushalten.why: Shipped 'hold out, stick out' is the literal physical sense, real but marginal; the verb is overwhelmingly reflexive — sich aus etwas heraushalten, halt dich da raus — candidate index 2, the sense a learner meets.
heraushalten.adjudicator_own_gloss: stay out of, keep out of

herausschreiben.why: English 'write out' reads as writing in full or in longhand; the German extracts by writing — copying quotations, figures, or vocabulary out of a source — which is what kaikki's '(i.e. of a work)' was pointing at.

herausstellen.why: The comma presents reflexive 'turn out' (candidate index 4) and transitive 'highlight' (candidate index 1) as synonyms; commit to the reflexive sich-herausstellen sense a learner meets constantly in es stellte sich heraus, dass ...

herausziehen.why: Shortening candidate index 0 'to pull (out)' dropped the parenthesized 'out', collapsing the gloss onto simplex ziehen; the heraus- prefix is the whole content of the verb — extraction (a splinter, a plug, a tooth).

hermachen.why: Shipped is ungrammatical ('a impression') and was cut from kaikki's 'to make a (specified) impression', losing the parenthetical that carried the meaning: the verb needs a quantifier (viel hermachen = look impressive) and is not the English idiom 'make an impression'.

herumkommen.why: Shipped literal 'move round something' (candidate index 0) is the least-used reading; the everyday idiom is um etwas nicht herumkommen — candidate index 2, being unable to avoid something (da kommst du nicht drum herum).

hervorsehen.why: The shortening dropped kaikki's '(of an object)' and left a bare transitive-looking 'show' (= zeigen); hervorsehen is intransitive — something protrudes into view, das Taschentuch sah aus der Jackentasche hervor (candidate index 0).

hinauslaufen.why: In modern German the verb is met almost exclusively in auf etwas hinauslaufen = amount to (candidate index 1, Das läuft auf dasselbe hinaus); the shipped literal sense is rarer and 'walk' mistranslates laufen (run).

hindeuten.why: Shipped 'point' takes the physical-gesture sense (for which German uses zeigen anyway); the reading a learner meets is the evidential one at candidate index 2 — alles deutet darauf hin, dass ... — indicate/suggest.

hinfahren.why: The importer took the rare transitive haben-sense (index 0, 'give a ride'), leaving the everyday intransitive sein-sense unparseable: a learner who meets 'ich fahre hin' cannot recover it from 'give a ride'. Proposed matches candidate_glosses index 1.

hingucken.why: The shipped 'synonym of hinsehen' is a Wiktionary cross-reference, not English about the verb, and must be replaced regardless; the proposed 'take a look, look' correctly renders the colloquial equivalent of hinsehen.
hingucken.adjudicator_own_gloss: look over there, take a look

hinrücken.why: Shortening candidate_glosses index 0 dropped the '(from speaker)' deixis and left 'move away', which reads as distancing (wegrücken/abrücken) — the opposite direction. Hinrücken shifts something toward a target; the proposal restores the hin- deixis.

hintanhalten.old: evite, try to make something not appear
hintanhalten.why: 'Evite' is an archaic Latinate rarity no learner will know and 'try to make something not appear' is a dictionary paraphrase, not a gloss — neither is usable English. 'Prevent, avert' is correct for this Austrian/administrative verb.

hintanstellen.old: put back, order into a posterior position
hintanstellen.why: 'Put back' misdirects to returning an object (zurückstellen) and 'order into a posterior position' is stilted dictionary English, not a gloss. 'Put last' cleanly names placing something last in priority (seine Interessen hintanstellen).

hinwegsehen.why: The importer took the literal index 0 ('look over'), which independently misleads in English toward 'examine'; the sense a learner meets is the figurative index 1, über etwas hinwegsehen = overlook/turn a blind eye. Proposed matches index 1.

hochdrehen.why: 'Turn upward' reads as orientation (rotate to point up), a different action from the verb's everyday meaning of increasing a setting or revving (die Heizung/den Motor hochdrehen). My independent gloss is 'turn up' before seeing the proposal; the shipped shortening misnames the action, not merely under-specifies it.

hochfahren.why: 'Drive upwards/northwards' is the marginal literal index 0 with an awkward slash forcing a choice between two unrelated directions; the salient modern sense is booting/ramping up (den Rechner hochfahren). Proposed matches candidate_glosses index 1.

hochrechnen.old: calculate purposefully high in the dark
hochrechnen.why: The importer took the pejorative index 1, and 'calculate purposefully high in the dark' is not usable English about anything. Hochrechnen is the neutral statistical verb behind Hochrechnung; candidate_glosses index 0 supplies 'to project, to cast'.

innehaben.why: Bare 'hold' presents the verb as a synonym of halten and invites '*ich habe das Buch inne'; innehaben takes offices and posts, never physical objects, and that restriction is the whole meaning. Candidate_glosses index 0 states it and house style permits the parenthetical.

kehren.why: The comma in 'sweep, turn' asserts synonymy between two unrelated actions, and 'turn' is not even in candidate_glosses, which lists only 'to sweep' (index 0). The living everyday sense is the southern counterpart to fegen.

klappen.why: 'Work out, fold' comma-joins two distinct senses (index 2 and index 1), which the house convention reads as equivalence; the constant learner sense is impersonal 'das klappt' = it works out/succeeds. Proposed keeps both halves of index 2, which are genuine synonyms.

kleinkriegen.why: Bare 'break' dropped the qualifier that carried the meaning and points at physical breakage (kaputtmachen/zerbrechen); candidate_glosses index 0 is 'to break (psychologically)', of wearing a person down. Proposed restores that restriction.

kontrollieren.why: 'Control, check' leads with the false friend and, under the house comma convention, asserts that control and check are synonyms — they are not (eine Firma kontrollieren = control it, not check it). The everyday sense is check/inspect (candidate_glosses index 0), which is also my independent gloss; the proposal replaces a false-synonymy pair with a true one.

leichtfallen.why: The comma in 'come, be easy' is a truncation artifact splitting the phrase 'come easy', so under the house convention it offers 'come' as a standalone sense the verb does not have. 'das fällt mir leicht' = that comes easily to me; the proposal fixes the split.

losschlagen.why: 'Knock loose' is the technical literal index 0 (Putz losschlagen) a learner will rarely meet; the ordinary sense is launching an attack (die Armee schlug los), at candidate_glosses indices 1 and 2. Proposed pairs two genuine synonyms.

mitbekommen.old: get or be given something when leaving
mitbekommen.why: The shipped index 0 ('given something when leaving') is real but marginal; the constant learner sense is catching or becoming aware of something (Hast du das mitbekommen?), candidate_glosses index 1, which shipping only the first-listed sense leaves unglossed.

mitfahren.why: 'Drive with' is a Germanism that attributes the driver's role, but mitfahren specifically means travelling as a passenger (Kann ich mitfahren?). That is a wrong-role defect, not mere imprecision; 'ride along' names the correct action.

mitkriegen.why: 'Synonym of mitbekommen' is a cross-reference that tells a learner nothing, and mitbekommen is itself mis-glossed in this corpus. Colloquial mitkriegen means to catch/notice/pick up on (Hast du das mitgekriegt?); the proposal states the meaning directly.

mitreißen.why: 'Entrain' is a fluid-dynamics term of art that otherwise means to board a train — useless or wrong for a learner. Mitreißen sweeps something along by force (der Fluss riss das Boot mit); candidate_glosses index 1 supplies 'to carry away'.

mitspielen.new: play along, join in a game
mitspielen.why: 'Cooperate' is the figurative extension (wenn das Wetter mitspielt) and collides with mitarbeiten/mitwirken; the everyday sense is taking part in a game, candidate_glosses index 1 'to play along'. Proposed names that sense.

nachblicken.why: 'Look at' names a different action (ansehen/anschauen); nachblicken is always jemandem nachblicken, following someone with one's eyes as they leave. The nach- deixis carries the whole meaning and is absent from the shipped gloss.

nachempfinden.why: Shipped 'feel for' is candidate index 1 and reads as pity/sympathy, colliding with mitfühlen; the core sense is index 0, imaginatively re-experiencing a feeling and so understanding it (Das kann ich gut nachempfinden). Proposed matches index 0 in house style.

nachsagen.old: repeat something said by someone else
nachsagen.why: The idiomatic 'jemandem etwas nachsagen' (say/impute something about someone, often unflattering) is candidate index 1 and the sense a learner actually meets; the shipped index-0 echo/parrot sense is handled in ordinary German by nachsprechen, which this shard glosses 'repeat'.

nachsetzen.why: Shipped 'place after' is the technical typographic sense (index 0); the everyday reading is candidate index 1, jemandem nachsetzen 'give chase' (die Polizei setzte dem Flüchtenden nach). Proposed restores the common sense.

niederstoßen.old: thrust down, knock down so that it falls)
niederstoßen.why: The shipped gloss ends 'knock down so that it falls)' with an unbalanced closing parenthesis, a truncation artifact spliced from candidate index 0's parenthetical clarifier. Proposed is the clean definition.

offenhalten.why: Shipped 'synonym of offenlassen' is a Wiktionary cross-reference, leaked apparatus that points to another German word rather than translating this one. The meaning sat in the same candidate index 0 ('...; to keep open'); proposed recovers it.

preisgeben.why: Shipped leads entirely with the literary abandon/surrender sense (candidate index 0, 'dem Untergang preisgeben'); the everyday sense a learner meets is candidate index 1, disclosing information (Daten/Details/Identität preisgeben). Wrong sense chosen when the common one was available.

raushalten.new: stay out of, keep out of
raushalten.why: 'hold out' reads in English as endure/resist (durchhalten), an action raushalten does not denote. In real use it is overwhelmingly reflexive, sich aus etwas raushalten / Halt dich da raus! — the clipping inherits heraushalten's keep-clear sense; proposed is correct even though kaikki lists only the literal reading.
raushalten.adjudicator_own_gloss: keep out of, stay out of

reinwaschen.why: The literal washing sense (candidate index 0) is marked rare; actual use is figurative, clearing someone of suspicion or laundering (sich von einem Verdacht reinwaschen, Geld reinwaschen), which is candidate index 1 'whitewash'. Shipped 'cleanse' also collides with reinigen.

richten.why: The comma in 'direct, judge' asserts synonymy between two unrelated senses; 'direct/aim/point' is the everyday sense (candidate index 0, den Blick auf etwas richten) while 'judge' is the elevated legal/biblical sense (index 5). Proposed 'direct, aim' keeps genuine synonyms.

sattsehen.old: have enough of seeing something beautiful
sattsehen.why: Shipped is candidate index 0 lifted verbatim; 'have enough of seeing something beautiful' reads in English as being fed up with the sight, inverting the positive satiation of sich nicht sattsehen können ('can't get enough of looking at it'), and it far exceeds house-style length. 'Look one's fill' is the standard idiom.

seligmachen.why: 'beatify' (candidate index 0) names the Church's act of declaring someone Blessed, which is seligsprechen — a distinct verb this corpus already glosses that way. seligmachen is selig + machen, to grant blessedness/salvation; kaikki conflated the neighbours and 'beatify' names an action this verb does not denote.

sorgen.why: Shipped leads with 'worry', the reflexive-only sense (candidate index 2) and itself uncommon beside sich Sorgen machen, comma-paired with the vague 'care'. The verb a learner meets is für etwas sorgen, candidate indices 0 and 1 (take care of / ensure), which proposed captures.

starkmachen.why: Shipped 'strengthen' is kaikki's literal stark+machen reading (candidate index 0) and collides with stärken, already glossed 'strengthen'. Real usage is reflexive advocacy, sich für etwas starkmachen, candidate index 1 'support, advocate for'.

thematisieren.why: 'make topic' is not English — a truncation of 'make a topic of' that lost its article and preposition, a fragment a learner cannot use. Candidate index 0 'bring up, address an issue' gives the sense cleanly.

umsteigen.why: The shortening dropped candidate index 0's meaning-carrying '(from one means of transport to another)', leaving three vague synonyms including the misleading 'interchange' (English: swap two things for each other), which umsteigen never means. Proposed restores the needed restriction in house style.

umstimmen.why: Shipped 'retune' is the technical musical sense (candidate index 0, ein Instrument umstimmen), essentially never met by a learner; the everyday sense is candidate index 1, jemanden umstimmen, to talk someone round. Technical sense chosen over the common one.

umtreiben.why: Shipped 'drive around' is the archaic agricultural sense (candidate index 0, driving livestock about); modern German uses umtreiben almost exclusively for what occupies or troubles the mind (Was treibt dich um?), candidate index 1. Archaic sense chosen over the current one.

umwenden.why: The comma presents 'turn over' and 'turn inside out' as synonyms, but they are different actions, and turning a garment inside out is umkrempeln/umstülpen. umwenden is turning something onto its other side (a page, a pancake); dropping the stray half removes the false synonymy.

unterfangen.why: The living verb is reflexive, sich unterfangen, to dare or have the audacity (candidate index 1, Wie kannst du dich unterfangen...). Shipped 'undertake' belongs to the noun das Unterfangen; as a verb it is archaic and steers a learner toward unterfangen where unternehmen is wanted.

untergehen.why: Bare 'set' is a fragment of candidate index 0 whose parenthetical '(of a heavenly body...)' carried the meaning; stripped, it reads as place/put/harden, none of which the verb does. The core is going down or under — sun setting, ship sinking, empire perishing — which proposed covers (senses at indices 0 and 4).

unterhalten.why: The comma equates two distinct senses, entertaining (candidate index 1) and maintaining a building/fleet (index 0), teaching that they are interchangeable renderings. Entertain is the sense a learner meets first, alongside the reflexive sich unterhalten 'converse'.

verabschieden.why: False-synonymy comma: 'say goodbye' (sich verabschieden, index 0) and 'pass' a law (index 4) are joined as if equivalent, which the house comma reads as synonyms. Committing to the everyday reflexive sense removes the misreading.

verbiegen.why: 'something' is kaikki's transitivity placeholder from index 0 ('to bend something.'), retained only to contrast with the intransitive index 1; it is dictionary scaffolding, not part of the meaning. Bare 'bend' is the attested sense.

verbuchen.why: Bare 'post' reads to a learner as posting mail or online, neither of which verbuchen means; the accounting sense is to book or record an entry. 'book' is candidate index 2 ('to register, book').

verfehlen.why: 'meet or hit not' is broken English carried verbatim from candidate index 0, a stranded calque of 'nicht treffen'. The leading 'miss' already renders the verb correctly; the trailing fragment is apparatus.

verhaften.why: Shipped 'stop moving and instead stick' is kaikki's literary paraphrase (index 0), both the wrong sense and unusable English. The everyday police sense is candidate index 1 ('to imprison, to put into confinement after judicial writ'): arrest.

verheiraten.why: 'marry (someone)' is heiraten's meaning and collapses the prefix: heiraten is what spouses do, verheiraten is what a third party does. Candidate index 1 has the distinctive sense: 'to marry off; to find a spouse for'.

verhelfen.why: Bare 'help' is exactly helfen and drops the ver- prefix; verhelfen is always jemandem zu etwas verhelfen. Kaikki's index 0 kept the frame as 'to help (to)', which the shortening lost, leaving a base-verb collapse.

verkehren.why: 'interact in someone's sphere' is leaked dictionary paraphrase naming no recognizable action. The everyday transport sense ('Die Linie verkehrt stündlich') is inside candidate index 0, buried after the paraphrase as 'to operate'.

verlauten.why: Bare verlauten is reportive and near-subjectless ('wie aus Regierungskreisen verlautet'); 'announce' is the meaning of the causative verlauten lassen, so the shipped gloss names an action the bare verb does not denote and teaches the wrong argument structure.

verleben.why: Verleben takes only time as its object ('den Sommer verleben'); bare 'spend' next to a German verb reads first as spending money, which is ausgeben. The parenthetical restriction removes the ambiguity.

verlernen.why: The importer took candidate index 1, whose 'cease doing' is aufhören's meaning, not verlernen's; and the house comma presents 'cease doing' and 'forget' as equivalents. Verlernen is losing a skill through disuse (index 0, 'lose the ability to do a task due to rarely doing it').

verloben.why: Leaked dictionary apparatus: the trailing "'someone'])" is the cut-off tail of kaikki's argument-structure note in candidate index 0, not English about the verb. Sich verloben means to become engaged.

verlöschen.why: The strong-verb form the app conjugates is intransitive ('die Kerze verlischt'); 'quench, extinguish' is transitive löschen/auslöschen and invites *ich verlösche das Feuer. The intransitive reading is candidate index 1 ('to go out, to fade').

verrechnen.why: The shortening kept the definitional first half of candidate index 0 and dropped the half that named the action ('particularly: to offset one against another'). 'calculate several quantities together' is a description a learner cannot substitute into 'etwas mit etwas verrechnen'.

verschlagen.why: Shipped kept an unfiltered synonym pile from candidate index 0: 'shlep' is an opaque Yiddish regionalism and 'bring' is too general to name anything. The live use is near-impersonal ('es hat ihn nach München verschlagen'), which 'strand' plus a directional carries.

versehen.why: 'equip, make mistake' welds two unrelated senses as house-style synonyms: transitive 'mit etwas versehen' (candidate index 3, 'to provide with') and the rare reflexive sich versehen (index 4). The common transitive sense is the one to ship.

verstoßen.why: 'violate, expel' pairs two different constructions as synonyms: 'gegen etwas verstoßen' (violate a rule, candidate index 1) and 'jemanden verstoßen' (disown, index 0). The first is far more frequent; 'violate, infringe' are true synonyms.

vertreiben.why: False-synonymy comma joins 'drive out' (candidate index 0) and the commercial 'distribute' (index 2), risking confusion with verteilen. Shipping the expulsion sense removes the false equivalence and sits beside the app's austreiben/verjagen.

verweisen.why: Same comma collision: 'refer' (auf etwas verweisen, candidate index 0) and 'expel' (von der Schule verweisen, index 2) are presented as synonyms. Referring is the commoner reading and governs the verb's usual prepositional frame.

vonstattengehen.why: 'take place' is stattfinden and invites *'Das Konzert geht vonstatten'; vonstattengehen describes how a process runs, almost always with a manner adverbial ('reibungslos vonstattengehen'). Candidate index 1 has it: 'to proceed'.

vorbilden.why: 'preform' is a technical/literal reading a learner will not meet and is easily misread as 'perform'. The everyday sense is preliminary training ('gut vorgebildet'), candidate index 1 ('to prelearn; to prepare; to equip with knowledge in advance').

vorbringen.why: The shortening dropped candidate index 0's qualifier ('to say in the sense of to allege or state'), leaving bare 'say' indistinguishable from sagen. Vorbringen specifically means to advance an argument, objection, or complaint ('Einwände vorbringen').

vorhalten.why: The dominant use is 'jemandem etwas vorhalten' = to reproach (candidate index 1), and the shipped bare 'hold up' invites the far commoner English readings 'delay' and 'rob', which the German verb never carries. The proposal restores an attested sense in usable English.

vorlesen.why: Shipped 'read' collapses the verb into its base lesen and loses the vor- component; vorlesen is specifically reading aloud to a listener. Matches candidate index 0, whose '(aloud)' parenthetical was dropped in shortening.

vorsetzen.why: 'Prefix' (candidate index 0) is a narrow grammatical/technical sense that misleads a learner toward morphology; the everyday sense is setting/serving something before someone (candidate indices 1 and 2), which the proposal restores.

vorsingen.why: Shipped 'sing' is identical in force to the base verb singen; the '(something to someone)' of candidate index 0 was stripped. vorsingen is singing for a listener, and by extension auditioning (index 1).

vorwerfen.why: The literal throwing sense (index 0) is now largely confined to the fixed image of throwing someone to the lions, while 'jemandem etwas vorwerfen' = accuse/reproach (candidate index 2) is one of the most frequent constructions in German news prose. The shipped gloss teaches the wrong action.

wegdrängen.why: The shipped 'edge away' is intransitive English (the subject retreats), but wegdrängen is transitive and forceful — to shove someone aside, to crowd out a competitor. The only candidate (index 0) is itself the mistranslation, and 'edge off' is not idiomatic English at all.

wegführen.why: wegführen is führen (lead), not tragen (carry): 'die Polizei führte den Mann weg'. The shipped 'carry away' names the wrong action and collides with wegtragen; the sole candidate inherits kaikki's error.

wehren.why: In modern German wehren is essentially reflexive — sich wehren, to defend oneself (candidate index 0). Bare 'defend' reads transitively and points a learner at verteidigen; adding 'oneself' restores the attested sense.

weismachen.why: The shipped 'make believe' is an English fixed phrase meaning to pretend or play imaginatively, the opposite kind of act. 'jemandem etwas weismachen' is to deceive someone into believing something untrue; the shipped gloss ships an English idiom, not the verb's meaning.

weiterarbeiten.why: 'resume' asserts an interruption that weiter- does not: 'arbeite weiter!' means keep at it, not start again. The rest of the weiter- cluster is glossed as continuation (weiterlesen, weiterleben), making the sole candidate 'resume one's work' the aspect outlier.

weiterkämpfen.old: continue to battle after a pause
weiterkämpfen.why: 'continue to battle' is right, but 'after a pause' is a false restriction imported from the dictionary line (the only candidate): weiterkämpfen is to fight on with or without an interruption, and the trailing clause also overruns house length badly.

wiedergeben.why: 'reproduce, return' joins two unrelated actions with a comma the house style reads as synonymy, and the give-back sense (index 0) is dated (modern German returns objects with zurückgeben). The live senses are rendering content (index 1) and playback (index 2), both covered by 'reproduce, render'.

wundern.why: Leading with 'wonder' teaches a false friend: wundern is transitive 'surprise, astonish' (candidate index 0) and reflexive 'be surprised' (index 1), never English 'wonder' in the sense of asking oneself, which is sich fragen. The proposal removes the false friend.

zerwerfen.why: 'Break by throwing' (index 0) is the regional literal sense and duplicates zerschmeißen exactly; the current standard use is reflexive 'sich mit jemandem zerwerfen' = to quarrel and break off relations (candidate index 1), which the proposal restores.

zeugen.why: The comma presents two unrelated senses as synonyms — begetting a child (index 0) and bearing witness (index 1). The transitive core is 'ein Kind zeugen'; 'testify' additionally misleads because courtroom testimony is aussagen. Ship the transitive sense.

zubringen.why: Shipped 'bring' collapses into the base verb bringen and names the regional herbeibringen sense that now survives mainly in the noun Zubringer. The everyday meaning is spending time somewhere — 'er brachte den Tag im Bett zu' — candidate index 1.

zufliegen.why: The '(toward)' of the sole candidate was dropped, leaving a gloss identical to plain fliegen. The directional zu- is the entire content of the verb, so 'fly toward' restores what distinguishes it.

zugreifen.why: The gloss leads with the computing sense (index 2) and comma-joins it to the physical sense, presenting two senses as synonyms. The everyday meaning is grabbing or seizing quickly (candidate index 0); 'access' should not head the gloss.

zuhalten.why: 'be keep something shut' is not English — the importer copied a malformed Wiktionary line (candidate index 0) verbatim. The verb means to hold something shut: die Tür zuhalten, sich die Nase zuhalten. This is a leaked truncation artifact, strong grounds.

zukehren.why: 'turn something' drops the directional zu- that is the verb's whole content, and kaikki's index 0 '(rotate)' pushes the wrong reading: zukehren is not rotating but turning a side toward someone — jemandem den Rücken zukehren. 'turn toward' captures the meaning.

zuleiten.why: The parenthetical that carried the meaning was dropped: kaikki index 0 is 'to feed (a liquid, electricity, etc.)', and bare 'feed' reads as füttern, which zuleiten never means. The verb channels or supplies along a conduit — Wasser, Strom zuleiten.

zunähen.why: 'suture' is a surgical term, but zunähen is the ordinary domestic word for sewing something closed — ein Loch, eine Naht zunähen. The register mismatch keeps a learner from using it where it belongs; candidate index 1 'stitch up' is the everyday equivalent.

zurichten.why: 'hurt' is a weak gloss the importer took at face value; the German for hurting someone is verletzen or wehtun. In current usage zurichten appears almost exclusively as 'übel/schlimm zurichten' = to batter or leave in a wrecked state, so 'hurt' invites badly wrong output.

zurufen.why: Bare 'call' collapses zurufen into its base rufen and drops the zu-, whose whole content is directing the call at someone across a distance; the German unambiguously carries that even though candidate_glosses only lists 'to call'. 'call out to' is correct and in house style.

zurückstehen.why: The shipped literal-spatial gloss ships the least-used sense, and 'stand behind' is a genuine false friend (an English speaker reads it as 'support', the opposite of the German). 'take a back seat' captures the dominant figurative restraint sense at candidate index 2.

zusammenbringen.why: 'collect' is the marginal index-0 reading and points at sammeln; the transparent core sense a learner meets — zwei Menschen zusammenbringen — is 'bring together' at candidate index 3.

zusammendrängen.why: 'condense' names only the figurative/transferred reading; the primary, mostly reflexive physical sense (sich zusammendrängen, to press into a small space) is candidate index 1 and is what a learner meets first.

zusammenfahren.why: The startle reaction (er fuhr zusammen) at candidate index 1 is the frequent, idiomatic sense; glossing this as 'collide' ships the rarer reading and points the learner away from zusammenstoßen, the normal word for a vehicle collision.

zusammennehmen.why: 'add up, total' corresponds only to the frozen adverbial 'alles zusammengenommen', not the live verb; gathering one's resources (Mut/Kräfte zusammennehmen) is candidate index 2.

zuschlagen.why: The physical strike sense (der Täter schlug zu) is candidate index 0, whose kaikki wording ('avail oneself of one's muscular power…') was unusable, so the importer skipped to the colloquial 'take one's chance' at index 1. 'strike, hit' restores the primary sense in usable English.

zutreiben.why: Bare 'drive' reads as operating a vehicle (fahren) and drops the zu-; zutreiben is to drive cattle/a boat toward a destination, or intransitively drift toward one. Candidate index 0 carries the directional complement the shortening stripped.

zuwenden.why: 'turn' is wenden/drehen and reads as rotating an object; zuwenden is to orient toward someone (sich ihm zuwenden), the directional content of the zu- prefix, at candidate index 2.

überarbeiten.why: The shipped comma presents 'overwork' as a synonym of 'revise', but overwork is the distinct reflexive sich überarbeiten (candidate index 1). Committing to the transitive revise/rework sense at index 0 removes a false equivalence that would tempt a learner to drop the obligatory reflexive pronoun.

überblicken.why: Both shipped items are broken: 'oversee' means supervise (beaufsichtigen) and 'overview' is not an English verb. überblicken means to take in the whole of something at a glance; the proposal is correct English even though kaikki reproduces only the two bad items.
überblicken.adjudicator_own_gloss: survey, take in at a glance

überführen.why: 'translate' is the narrow ecclesiastical relic/see sense imported unfiltered from candidate index 0, and sitting next to the real 'translate' verb übersetzen it actively invites a false equivalence. The remaining three items render the transport sense correctly.

übergehen.why: The entry ships as inseparable (überging, hat übergangen), whose sense is skip/pass over/ignore (candidate indices 0 and 1); 'go over to' is the separable ÜBERgehen with a different conjugation, so the comma joins two distinct verbs and must be dropped for the inseparable entry.

überhören.why: 'mishear' is wrong and collides with sich verhören (to hear something incorrectly); überhören is to not register an utterance at all, accidentally or deliberately (candidate index 0, minus the dropped '(deliberately)' that made the source barely defensible).

überkommen.why: 'conquer, seize' name überwinden/besiegen and reverse the argument structure — in überkommen the feeling is subject and the person object (mich überkam die Angst), so the shipped gloss would produce wrong German like *ich überkam meine Angst. 'come over, overwhelm' has the right direction; 'overwhelm' is candidate index 1.

überlassen.why: 'abandon' names verlassen/aufgeben and only surfaces in the fixed 'jemanden seinem Schicksal überlassen', too narrow to carry the gloss; both candidate glosses describe only relinquishing-to-someone, which 'entrust to' renders correctly.

überschauen.why: English 'overlook' is dominantly read as 'fail to notice' — which is übersehen — so it teaches the opposite of überschauen. The verb means to take in and comprehend the whole; 'to grasp, to assess, to comprehend' is candidate index 1.

überschreiben.why: 'make over, sign over (property)' is the specialized legal-conveyancing sense at candidate index 0; the sense a learner overwhelmingly meets is the computing one (Datei überschreiben) at candidate indices 2 and 3. Shipping the notary sense over the everyday one is choosing a technical reading where a common one was available.

überspielen.why: 'sth' is a dictionary abbreviation for 'something' that survived the import (candidate index 0) — apparatus, not English — leaving the gloss reading as an unfinished phrase. The dubbing sense is correct and just needs the placeholder removed.
